title: UEG Week 2026: Young Co-Chair and three abstract presentations
summary: Young Co-Chair of the moderated poster session “Therapeutics in IBD: Real-world experience (I)”, plus three accepted abstracts on NLP/LLM-based Montreal classification, transient elastography in heart failure, and a clinical case of clear cell sarcoma of the gastrointestinal tract.
abstract:
**Faculty role.** Young Co-Chair, moderated poster session *Therapeutics in IBD: Real-world experience (I)*, Tuesday 20 October 2026, 11:30-12:30.

**Presentations**

- Automated extraction of the Montreal classification from endoscopy reports with NLP and large language models (poster, Saturday 17 October).
- Clear cell sarcoma of the gastrointestinal tract presenting as obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (clinical case poster UEG2026:1362, Saturday 17 October).
- Liver stiffness by transient elastography in heart failure: linking hepatic congestion with echocardiographic findings (moderated poster, Tuesday 20 October).

title: NLP-based classification of bowel preparation quality in colonoscopy reports
summary: Poster Mo2176: automated bowel-preparation quality classification over 11,374 colonoscopy reports (TF-IDF + logistic regression, ~92% accuracy), selected for the AGA Innovation Themed Walking Tour.
abstract: Poster presentation (Mo2176) of an NLP pipeline that classifies bowel-preparation quality from free-text colonoscopy reports (11,374 reports; TF-IDF + logistic regression; ~92% cross-validated accuracy). Selected for the AGA Innovation Themed Walking Tour.

title: NLP-based classification of bowel preparation quality and its association with adenoma detection rate
summary: Late-breaking oral presentation: NLP classification of bowel-preparation quality (TF-IDF + logistic regression, 92% CV accuracy, 11,374 reports) and its association with adenoma detection rate (n = 5,420; ADR 20.4%).
abstract: Late-breaking oral presentation. A natural-language-processing model (TF-IDF + logistic regression) classified bowel-preparation quality in 11,374 free-text colonoscopy reports with 92% cross-validated accuracy; the derived labels were then linked to adenoma detection in 5,420 screening/diagnostic colonoscopies (ADR 20.4%).
